title: Environmental / Fuel Economy: Jeep Compass page claims 'up to 30 mpg' without an EPA-estimate qualifier
quote: New 2026 Jeep Compass (VIN 3C4NJDBN8TT235093) description: 'Enjoy up to 30 mpg highway efficiency', while the same page lists 23/31 City/Highway MPG.
recommendation: Label every mileage claim as an EPA estimate and match the EPA figures on the page, for example 'EPA-estimated 31 mpg highway. Actual mileage will vary.' The description copy on the Compass page should be corrected or removed.

title: CCPA/CPRA Privacy: Privacy policy does not mention Global Privacy Control or browser opt-out signals
quote: Privacy policy does not mention Global Privacy Control or browser opt-out signals.
statute: Cal. Civ. Code §1798.135(e), CPRA; 11 CCR §7025
recommendation: Disclose whether and how the business honors Global Privacy Control (GPC) browser signals.

title: CARS Act Total-Payable Disclosure: Jeep Compass detail page shows a monthly payment without the total amount payable
quote: New 2026 Jeep Compass (VIN 3C4NJDBN8TT235093): Estimated Finance Payment $447/mo. for 84 months, APR 5.90%, with no total of payments shown.
statute: Cal. Civ. Code §1784.41(c)(1) (CARS Act, SB 766) | CALIFORNIA controls: CARS Act (SB 766, Cal. Civ. Code §1784.20 et seq.), operative Oct 1, 2026. The federal FTC CARS Rule (16 CFR Part 463) was VACATED by the 5th Circuit (Jan 2025) and formally WITHDRAWN from the CFR (Fed. Reg. Feb 2026), not enforceable; FTC Section 5 still applies. Pin-cites verified against the chaptered statute (leginfo) 2026-06-28; CNCDA Compliance Guide v1.2 (2026-08-07) and Webinar FAQ (2026-08-31) folded in 2026-09-14.
recommendation: The California CARS Act (SB 766) takes effect October 1, 2026. Any monthly payment shown on a vehicle page must also show the total the customer will have paid after all payments, plus any assumed down payment or trade value, and the vehicle's total price. For the Compass, $447 x 84 months is $37,548 before any down payment. Ask Pixel Motion to add a total-of-payments line under the payment calculator on every detail page, or show total price only and quote payments after desking (CNCDA Compliance Guide guidance).

title: OEM Brand Guidelines: New inventory page title 'New Inventory for Sale | Anaheim, CA' has no brand name
quote: New inventory page title: 'New Inventory for Sale | Anaheim, CA' (no Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep or Ram).
statute: Stellantis Website Guidelines / Dealer Advertising Program — Website: Certified Website Provider
recommendation: Ask Pixel Motion to change the new inventory page title to name the brands, for example 'New Chrysler, Dodge, Jeep, Ram Inventory for Sale | Anaheim, CA'.

title: Accessibility (ADA/Unruh): 25 of 104 homepage images missing alt text
quote: 25 of 104 homepage images missing alt text.
statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1 1.1.1
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: 25 of the 104 images on the homepage have no alt text, so screen readers cannot describe them. Some may be decorative and correctly empty. Ask Pixel Motion to add short descriptions to every meaningful image (vehicle photos, offer banners, buttons) and mark purely decorative images as decorative.

title: Accessibility (ADA/Unruh): 5 of 10 form fields have no associated label/aria-label
quote: 5 of 10 form fields have no associated label/aria-label.
statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1 1.3.1/4.1.2
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: 5 of the 10 form fields on the homepage have no label a screen reader can announce. Ask Pixel Motion to give every lead form field a visible or screen-reader label (name, email, phone, message) so shoppers using assistive technology can complete the form.

title: Accessibility (ADA/Unruh): Homepage structure gaps: no skip-to-content link (WCAG 2.4.1)
quote: Homepage structure gaps: no skip-to-content link (WCAG 2.4.1).
statute: ADA Title III; Cal. Civ. Code §51 (Unruh); WCAG 2.1
recommendation: Add a skip-to-main-content link. A quick fix that closes easy ADA/Unruh exposure.

title: Vehicle detail pages labeled 'Certified Pre Owned' in page title and social share title (2 of 4 sampled)
quote: <title>Certified Pre Owned Chrysler Dodge Jeep RAM</title> and og:title on USED 2018 TOYOTA HIGHLANDER XLE (Stock UK0015) and NEW 2026 JEEP CHEROKEE LAREDO 4X4 (Stock T0514)
statute: CA Vehicle Code §11713.18; CA B&P Code §17500
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The detail page title and social share title read 'Certified Pre Owned Chrysler Dodge Jeep RAM' on 2 of the 4 vehicle pages we sampled: a used 2018 Toyota Highlander with 171,787 miles and a new 2026 Jeep Cherokee. That is the text Google results and text-message link previews show. California only allows 'certified' on used vehicles that passed a real certification program. This was flagged in August on one used RAM 2500. Ask Pixel Motion to set every detail page title to the real year, make, model and trim, and keep 'Certified' only on true CPO units. To confirm, paste a detail page link into a text message and read the preview.

title: Used Durango shows an 'MSRP' and a 'Net Price' higher than its 'Sale Price'
quote: Net Price $22,820 | MSRP $22,735.00 | Sale Price: $22,735
statute: CA Civil Code §1784.41(a) (CA-CARS-025, operative 10/1/2026); CA Vehicle Code §11713.1; FTC Act §5
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The used 2024 Dodge Durango GT Plus (Stock UR0046, VIN 1C4RDHDG7RC189971) shows three prices that do not agree. An 'MSRP' of $22,735 appears on a used car, where MSRP does not apply and hints at a factory-new price. The 'Net Price' of $22,820 is $85 more than the 'Sale Price' of $22,735, so the lowest number reads like the price and the real number reads like a discount. The $85 gap may be the document processing charge, which the page does not say. Fix before October 1: remove the MSRP label from used vehicles, show one price labeled as the total price, and if the $85 is the doc fee, say so next to it (for example 'Total price $22,820, includes $85 document processing charge'). Check other used units for the same template problem.

title: Payment disclaimer on used Durango has a blank loan term
quote: exclude tax, license, handling, and doc fees, for  months.
statute: Regulation Z 12 CFR §1026.24(d); CA Civil Code §1784.41(c) (operative 10/1/2026); FTC Act §5
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The payment tool on the used Durango (Stock UR0046) prints the loan term as a blank ('for  months'), and the cash tab reads 'for 0 months'. Last month the same tool showed '0 months'. A payment with no term is an incomplete credit ad, and from October 1 every advertised payment also needs the total the buyer will pay over the loan. Have Pixel Motion hide the payment tool on any vehicle that has no rate and term loaded, or load a real term, rate, and total of payments for used units. The blank term sits inside the Finance and Lease tabs, so confirm on the live page which tabs a shopper can see.

title: New vehicle Net Price stacks bonus cash rebates with a 0% APR payment
quote: Retail Bonus Cash: − $2,500 | Bonus Cash: − $2,000 | Net Price: $33,709 | $476/mo. exclude tax, license, handling, and doc fees, for 72 months. | APR: 0.00% | Factory rebates may not be available if you choose special APR financing or lease programs.
statute: FTC Pricing Transparency FAQs Q5, Q9; CA Vehicle Code §11713.1; FTC Act §5
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The new 2026 Jeep Cherokee Laredo page stacks a $2,011 'McPeeks Discount', $2,500 National Retail Bonus Cash and $2,000 National Bonus Cash (both expiring 09/30/2026) to reach a $33,709 Net Price, and shows a $476/mo payment at 0.00% APR for 72 months. The site's own disclaimer says factory rebates may not be available with special APR financing, so a buyer may not get both. Show the payment on the price the buyer can actually get with that APR, say which rebates cannot be combined, and name who qualifies for each rebate next to the Net Price.

title: Specials 'net selling price' includes manufacturer rebates the site says customers may not qualify for
quote: Includes $4,500 in applicable manufacturer rebates and $2,799 McPeek’s Anaheim discount for a net selling price of $37,496. | Customer may not qualify for ALL Rebates shown. Some rebates are stackable and others can and cannot be combined.
statute: FTC Pricing Transparency FAQs Q5, Q9; CA Vehicle Code §11713.1; CA Civil Code §1784.41 (operative 10/1/2026)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: All five priced September specials (Wrangler, Compass, Pacifica, Charger, Ram 1500) build a 'net selling price' that already subtracts $2,500 to $6,730 in manufacturer rebates, without naming the rebates or who qualifies. The site footer then admits a customer may not qualify for all rebates shown. A shopper who does not qualify cannot buy at the advertised number. Fix: name each rebate and its eligibility in the offer, show the price a buyer gets without conditional rebates, and relabel the after-rebate figure as 'net cost after rebates' rather than 'net selling price' (CNCDA guidance treats an after-rebate figure called a 'price' as noncompliant from October 1).

title: Homepage offers show two different expiration dates
quote: Offer expires 10/1/2026. Expires: 10/02/2026
statute: CA Vehicle Code §11713.1; CA Civil Code §1784.41 (operative 10/1/2026); FTC Act §5
recommendation: Every homepage special (Ram 1500 Rebel 20% off, Jeep Wrangler, Chrysler Pacifica) says 'Offer expires 10/1/2026' and then 'Expires: 10/02/2026' in the same disclaimer. The rebates inside those prices also end sooner: the matching Compass stack on the detail page reads 'Exp. 09/30/2026'. A customer who walks in on October 1 or 2 could be told the price is gone. Set one end date in the offer tool, and make it no later than the earliest rebate expiration (9/30/2026) or note that rebate amounts may change after 9/30.

title: 'Closeout' specials headline used on current 2026 model-year offers
quote: NEW VEHICLE CLOSEOUT SPECIALS
statute: CA B&P Code §17501; FTC Act §5
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The homepage slider says 'NEW VEHICLE CLOSEOUT SPECIALS', but every offer behind it is a 2026 model, which is the current model year. 'Closeout' tells shoppers the store is clearing out the last units at a price that will not come back. Unless these are true final-unit prices on outgoing models, change the banner to 'New Vehicle Specials' or 'September Specials'. If 2027 models are already on the lot and these really are year-end clearance units, keep the word but add the end date.

title: Every used vehicle carries an undated 'Sale Price'
quote: USED 2021 CHRYSLER PACIFICA TOURING L ... Sale Price: $14,788
statute: CA B&P Code §17501; FTC Guides Against Deceptive Pricing 16 CFR §233.1
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: All 20 used listings we captured (page 1 of 3; the site shows 53 used vehicles), the certified page, and the used detail pages label the only price shown as 'Sale Price', with no former price and no end date. This was also flagged in August, so it reads as a permanent label rather than a real sale. California only allows 'sale' for a real, temporary reduction from a price the car was actually offered at. Change the used inventory label to 'Price' or 'Our Price', and use 'Sale' only on units with a documented prior price and a stated end date. Confirm with the used car manager that these are standing prices.

title: Price quote forms offer a better 'No BS Price' in exchange for contact details with no financial incentive notice
quote: Please fill out your information to receive your No BS Price! What does "No BS Price" mean? It means no addendums, no markups, no hidden fees.
statute: CA Civil Code §1798.125(b); 11 CCR §7016 (CCPA notice of financial incentive)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: Site-wide price forms ('Get a Quick Quote', and the 'GET TODAY'S PRICE' button on new, used, certified, and detail pages) promise a price in return for name, phone, and email. Under California privacy rules, trading a price benefit for personal information is a financial incentive that needs a short notice at the form explaining the deal and how the value was set. The forms carry texting consent language but no such notice. Fix: either add a one-paragraph notice of financial incentive with a link to the privacy policy on these forms, or show the same price publicly and rename the button 'Check Availability'. Also from October 1, any price sent back must match the price posted on the site. The forms load in pop-ups, so confirm on the live site what text sits next to the submit button.

title: Homepage email sign-up field has no privacy notice at collection
quote: Enter your email | Sign Up
statute: CA Civil Code §1798.100(a); 11 CCR §7012
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The 'My Vehicles' sign-up on the homepage collects an email address with no privacy policy link or notice next to the field. The cookie banner covers some of this site-wide, so the risk is low. Add one line under the field, such as 'We collect your email to save your vehicles. See our Privacy Policy', with the link. The field sits in a pop-up panel, so confirm the current wording on the live site.

title: Homepage and specials offer disclaimers sit behind click-to-expand buttons
quote: Show Disclaimer
statute: CA Vehicle Code §11713.16(i); FTC Act §5 (clear and conspicuous)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: Our crawler had to click 10 disclaimer buttons on the specials page, and the homepage slider shows six 'Show Disclaimer' buttons, before the rebate, price, and expiration terms appeared. Terms that change the price should sit right under the price, not behind a click. Have the provider display each offer's disclaimer open by default under the offer, at least the rebate amounts and the end date. We cannot see the layout, so confirm on desktop and phone.

title: Inventory list lease payments show due-at-signing with terms behind a 'Disclaimer' link
quote: Lease $494/Month For 48 Months $3,875 Due at Signing Disclaimer
statute: Regulation M 12 CFR §1013.7; CA Civil Code §1784.41(c) (operative 10/1/2026); FTC Pricing Transparency FAQs Q8
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: New inventory cards show lease payments (for example $494 a month for 48 months, $3,875 due at signing on Compass Stock T0147) with the remaining lease terms behind a 'Disclaimer' link. There are no lease specials this month, but these per-vehicle lease payments are still ads. Confirm with the provider that the due-at-signing amount includes the first payment, acquisition fee, and doc fee, that the popup states security deposit, mileage limit, and total of lease payments, and move the total of payments next to the monthly figure before October 1.

title: Used vehicle pages do not mention the upcoming 3-day right to cancel
quote: Prices do not include government fees and taxes, finance charges, or emission testing charges for used vehicles.
statute: CA Civil Code §1784.50 et seq. (CARS Act, operative 10/1/2026)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: Starting October 1, used vehicles priced at $50,000 or less come with a 3-day right to cancel. The used listing page, certified page, and used detail pages have a used-vehicle disclaimer block but say nothing about it. Nothing on the pages contradicts the right, so this is a best-practice fix. Before October 1, add one sentence to the used disclaimer block: 'Used vehicles with a cash price of $50,000 or less purchased on or after October 1, 2026 include a 3-day right to cancel under California law. See dealer for details.' Our text capture may not include every footer, so confirm on the live pages.

title: Cookie banner says using the site means agreeing to a privacy policy with an arbitration provision
quote: By continuing to use this site, you agree to our Privacy Policy, which includes an Arbitration Provision
statute: CA Civil Code §1784.20 et seq. (CARS Act waiver prohibition, operative 10/1/2026)
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: The site-wide cookie banner says simply using the site means agreeing to an arbitration provision. The CARS Act voids any waiver of its protections. We did not see the arbitration text itself, so we cannot say whether it reaches vehicle purchase disputes. Ask ComplyAuto or the store's counsel to confirm the arbitration clause is limited to website and privacy matters and does not cover vehicle sales or CARS Act rights, and to add a line saying so.

title: Payment disclaimers exclude 'handling' fees while quote forms promise no hidden fees
quote: exclude tax, license, handling, and doc fees
statute: CA Civil Code §1784.41(a) (operative 10/1/2026); FTC Pricing Transparency FAQs Q6; FTC Act §5
recommendation: NEEDS HUMAN REVIEW: Every payment on the new and used detail pages says it excludes a 'handling' fee, while the quote form promises 'no addendums, no markups, no hidden fees'. From October 1 the advertised total price can leave out only government fees, finance charges, the document processing charge, and emission testing. If McPeek's does not charge a handling fee, have the provider remove the word 'handling' from the payment tool. If it does, it must be built into the advertised price.

title: Privacy policy page contains unfinished template text and a 2025 effective date
quote: contacting us directly at [Insert Contact Information]
statute: CA Civil Code §1798.130(a)(5); 11 CCR §7011
recommendation: The 'Privacy Policy & Notice of Collection' page still shows the unfilled template field '[Insert Contact Information]' where customers are told how to opt out of texts and emails, and its effective date is January 1, 2025. California requires the policy to be reviewed and updated at least every 12 months. Ask ComplyAuto to fill in the store's phone number and email and republish with a current date. The footer 'Privacy' link redirects to this same page, so one fix covers it.
